title: Outlier-Robust Multi-Output Gaussian Processes
claim: A single outlier in one output distorts a standard multi-output model's fit, while the robust variant stays unaffected.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels, shared x-axis, red outlier dot in left panel
description: Two side-by-side line plots share a Viability y-axis and a single x-axis label, Navitoclax Dose (log10 µM). The left panel is titled P12-ICHIKAWA (y1) and the right panel ARH-77 (y2). Each panel shows black scatter points of dose-response data that fall in a sigmoidal decline. A green curve with a wide pale-green uncertainty band is the standard MOGP, and a blue curve with a tighter blue band is the robust R-MOGP. In the left panel a single red outlier dot sits far above the trend near dose 0. It pulls the green MOGP curve upward and widens its band. The blue curve ignores it. In the right panel the curves nearly coincide, which shows the outlier's effect on the correlated output is small. The legend sits at the lower right of the right panel. The eye goes first to the red dot and the diverging green and blue curves.
caption: {Navitoclax dose-response with outlier.} We show the viability of two cancer cell lines exposed to varying doses of the drug Navitoclax.
abstract: Multi-output Gaussian process (MOGP) regression allows modelling dependencies among multiple correlated response variables. Similarly to standard Gaussian processes (GPs), MOGPs are sensitive to model misspecification and outliers, which can distort predictions within individual outputs. In the multi-output case, this situation can be further exacerbated as anomalous observations in one response can adversely influence predictions for other correlated outputs. To handle this situation, we propose R-MOGP, an MOGP that is provably robust to outliers in any individual response. Our approach preserves conjugacy, achieving robustness without sacrificing computational efficiency, and integrates naturally with sparse variational inference for scalability. Empirically, we show that R-MOGP achieves performance comparable to existing state-of-the-art robust MOGPs at a fraction of their computational costs.
